expected.note: American Opportunity credit disallowed entirely (student less than half time; payment by taxpayers not shown); Lifetime Learning credit also not allowed for lack of substantiated payment (fn. 6)
expected.snippet: For two independently sufficient reasons, we conclude that petitioners are not entitled to the education credit they claim.

expected.note: claimed refundable American Opportunity Credit disallowed entirely
expected.snippet: petitioners have failed to demonstrate their entitlement to any education credit for the year in issue.
Respondent further concedes that petitioners are not liable for an accuracy-related penalty under sec. 6662(a) for the year in issue.

issues_outside_coverage: Unreimbursed employee business expenses of $23,169 (Form 2106 / Schedule A) disallowed in full: petitioners did not show the expenses were not reimbursable by the employer (also insufficient sec. 274(d) substantiation)
Respondent's concession of $1,200 charitable cash contributions deduction
decisive_judgment_findings: Form 1098-T and Mr. Pichardo's testimony show he was a less-than-half-time student at UCSD Extension in 2016.
Tuition was paid with an employer-approved business credit card; no evidence that petitioners personally paid the card bills or that LPS did not reimburse them.
Mr. Pichardo had a right to reimbursement from LPS on substantiation and never sought it; no credible evidence which expenses were not reimbursable.

unscored_items.note: value omitted: decision under Rule 155 (respondent conceded a $1,200 charitable deduction); the court gives no final deficiency figure (notice deficiency was $5,348)
unscored_items.snippet: To reflect the foregoing conclusions and respondent's concessions, Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
